issues.description: Sensitive payment card data (cardNumber, cvv) stored in plain interface without encryption or PCI-DSS compliance markers
issues.suggestion: Never store raw card numbers or CVVs in application code. Use payment gateway tokens (Stripe, PayPal) instead. If PCI compliance is required, card data must be encrypted in transit and at rest, and should never be logged or stored in application database.

issues.description: Credit card data potentially logged in error handler via console.error which may expose sensitive payment information
issues.suggestion: Remove sensitive data from error logs. Replace 'console.error('Payment failed:', error)' with proper error logging that excludes PII/PCI data: 'logger.error('Payment processing failed', { errorCode: error.code })'

issues.description: SQL query vulnerable to potential issues if db.query doesn't use parameterized queries correctly. Also storing card data (even last 4 digits) requires PCI compliance
issues.suggestion: Verify db.query uses proper parameterized queries. Consider using an ORM like Prisma or TypeORM for type safety. Document PCI-DSS compliance requirements for storing payment data.

issues.description: SQL injection risk if JSON.stringify(features) contains malicious data, though parameterized query provides some protection
issues.suggestion: While parameterized queries help, validate the features array before serialization: 'const sanitizedFeatures = features.filter(f => typeof f === 'string' && /^[a-z_]+$/.test(f));'

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length, doesn't validate if it's numeric or use Luhn algorithm for card validation
issues.suggestion: Add proper validation: 'if (!/^\d{13,19}$/.test(cardNumber)) return false; if (!luhnCheck(cardNumber)) return false;' and implement Luhn algorithm or use a library like 'card-validator'.

issues.description: Date comparison bug - expiry date should be end of month, not beginning. A card expiring '12/25' is valid through Dec 31, 2025, not Dec 1, 2025
issues.suggestion: Fix to: 'const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0); // Last day of expiry month' or add 1 to month for first day of next month comparison.

issues.description: Year 2100 bug - using '2000 +' assumes years 00-99 map to 2000-2099, will fail after 2099
issues.suggestion: Use smarter logic: 'const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear() % 100; const century = year < currentYear - 10 ? 2100 : 2000; const fullYear = century + parseInt(year);'

issues.description: chargeCard function simulates payment but doesn't actually integrate with real payment gateway - dangerous for production
issues.suggestion: Implement actual payment gateway integration (Stripe, Braintree, etc.): 'const result = await stripe.charges.create({ amount: amount * 100, currency: 'usd', source: paymentToken });' Never process raw card data.

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess returns false if database query returns empty array, but doesn't distinguish between 'no subscription' and 'database error'
issues.suggestion: Add proper error handling: 'if (!rows || rows.length === 0) { return false; }' and wrap in try-catch to handle database errors separately from missing subscriptions.

issues.description: JSON.parse without try-catch can crash the application if features column contains invalid JSON
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: 'try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch (e) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON', { userId }); return false; }'

issues.description: JSON.parse without try-catch can crash the application if features column contains invalid JSON
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: 'try { features: JSON.parse(row.features) } catch (e) { logger.error('Invalid features JSON'); features: [] }'

issues.description: Payment amount comparison uses floating-point arithmetic which can cause precision errors (e.g., 9.99 !== 9.989999999)
issues.suggestion: Use integer arithmetic for money: convert to cents. 'if (payment.amount * 100 < amount * 100)' or use a decimal library like 'decimal.js' or 'big.js'.

issues.description: No rollback mechanism if upgradeUserSubscription fails after payment succeeds - user charged but not upgraded
issues.suggestion: Implement transaction pattern or compensating transaction: 'try { const charge = await chargeCard(); await upgradeUserSubscription(); } catch (e) { await refundCharge(charge.id); throw e; }'

issues.description: Hardcoded tax rate and processing fee - should be configurable and potentially vary by region/jurisdiction
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: 'const config = await getPaymentConfig(userId); const tax = basePrice * config.taxRate; const fee = basePrice * config.processingFee;'

issues.description: Database query executed every time hasFeatureAccess is called - should implement caching for subscription data
issues.suggestion: Add caching layer: 'const cached = await cache.get(`subscription:${userId}`); if (cached && cached.validUntil > Date.now()) return cached; const subscription = await db.query(...); await cache.set(`subscription:${userId}`, subscription, TTL);'

issues.description: getUserSubscription duplicates database query logic from hasFeatureAccess - code duplication and missed caching opportunity
issues.suggestion: Extract shared logic: 'async function fetchSubscription(userId: string) { /* query with caching */ } and reuse in both hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription.

issues.description: No input validation for userId parameter - could be empty string, null, or SQL injection attempt
issues.suggestion: Add validation: 'if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string' || !/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$/.test(userId)) { throw new Error('Invalid userId'); }'

issues.description: Using console.error instead of proper logging framework - makes monitoring and debugging difficult in production
issues.suggestion: Use structured logging: 'import { logger } from './logger'; logger.error('Payment processing failed', { userId, amount, errorCode: error.code });'

issues.description: Features array duplicated between premium and enterprise tiers - violates DRY principle
issues.suggestion: Define features configuration: 'const TIER_FEATURES = { base: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise_only: ['api_access', 'team_collaboration'] }; const features = tier === 'enterprise' ? [...TIER_FEATURES.base, ...TIER_FEATURES.enterprise_only] : TIER_FEATURES.base;'

issues.description: Magic numbers for pricing - should be in configuration or database to allow dynamic pricing changes
issues.suggestion: Move to config: 'const PRICING_CONFIG = { premium: { basePrice: 9.99, taxRate: 0.08, processingFee: 0.029 }, enterprise: { basePrice: 49.99, taxRate: 0.08, processingFee: 0.029 } };'

issues.description: CVV length validation accepts both 3 and 4 digits but doesn't validate it's numeric
issues.suggestion: Add numeric check: 'if (!/^\d{3,4}$/.test(cvv)) return false;'

issues.description: Date comparison using 'new Date()' called twice in hasFeatureAccess function - minor inefficiency
issues.suggestion: Store in variable: 'const now = new Date(); if (validUntil < now) return false;'

issues.description: Function lacks comprehensive JSDoc documentation for parameters, return values, and error conditions
No unit tests as noted in comments - critical business logic without test coverage is high risk
issues.suggestion: Create comprehensive test suite covering: valid/invalid payments, edge cases (expired cards, insufficient amounts), error scenarios, and subscription upgrades. Use Jest or Vitest with mocked database calls.

codeQuality.summary: Critical security vulnerabilities detected in payment processing code. The file handles sensitive PCI data (card numbers, CVV) insecurely, lacks proper payment gateway integration, has SQL injection risks, missing error handling for JSON parsing, and contains date validation bugs. Performance issues include lack of caching and code duplication. Missing tests for critical financial logic is extremely dangerous for production.

untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call processPremiumPayment('user123', {cardNumber: '123', expiryDate: 'invalid', cvv: '1', amount: 10.00}, 'premium') and expect it to throw Error with message 'Invalid payment details'

untestedPaths.reasoning: Must prevent subscription upgrades when payment amount is insufficient to avoid giving away premium features without proper payment.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Call processPremiumPayment('user123', {cardNumber: '1234567890123456', expiryDate: '12/25', cvv: '123', amount: 1.00}, 'premium') and expect it to throw Error with message 'Insufficient payment amount'

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage on payment processing and subscription management logic. All 5 exported functions and 3 internal functions are completely untested. This includes critical payment processing (processPremiumPayment, chargeCard), payment validation (validatePaymentDetails), pricing calculations (calculateSubscriptionPrice), subscription management (upgradeUserSubscription), and access control (hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription). Top priorities: test payment validation edge cases (expired cards, invalid formats), payment processing failures, pricing accuracy, subscription upgrades, and feature access control. Without tests, bugs could result in financial losses, security vulnerabilities, or customer trust issues.

suggestions.description: Introduce Strategy Pattern for payment processing and Repository Pattern for database operations to separate concerns and improve testability
suggestions.benefits: Separates database logic from business logic, makes code testable with dependency injection, follows SOLID principles, and allows easy swapping of payment gateways

suggestions.description: Extract expiry date validation logic into separate function to reduce complexity and improve reusability
suggestions.benefits: Each validation function has a single responsibility, easier to test individually, more readable, and validation logic can be reused elsewhere

suggestions.description: Use const for configuration objects and add decimal precision handling for monetary calculations
suggestions.benefits: Constants at module level are easier to configure and test, 'as const' provides stronger type safety, proper rounding prevents floating-point precision issues with monetary values

suggestions.description: Extract feature mapping to a const Record with proper typing and use modern date manipulation
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates ternary operator for better readability, centralizes feature configuration, makes date calculation reusable and testable, uses proper TypeScript Record type

suggestions.description: Extract subscription validation logic to reduce duplication and improve consistency
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplicate database query and subscription parsing logic, consolidates validation logic into reusable function, reduces chance of inconsistencies

suggestions.description: Improve error handling with proper typed error result instead of boolean return and console.error
suggestions.benefits: Removes console.error anti-pattern, provides structured error information to caller, allows proper logging at higher level, includes transaction ID for tracking, enables better error handling in processPremiumPayment

suggestions.description: Use early returns and optional chaining for cleaner control flow and update to work with new PaymentResult type
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling pattern (returns instead of throws for validation), provides detailed error information to caller, maintains transaction ID throughout the flow, easier to handle errors gracefully in consuming code

suggestions.description: Use parseInt with explicit radix parameter to avoid potential issues
suggestions.before:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1);
suggestions.after:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year, 10), parseInt(month, 10) - 1);
suggestions.benefits: Explicit radix prevents potential issues with octal interpretation in edge cases, follows ESLint best practices

suggestions.description: Add Value Object pattern for sensitive card data with validation and security best practices
suggestions.benefits: Encapsulates card number validation and formatting, prevents accidental exposure of full card numbers, provides type-safe access to card data, centralizes security-sensitive logic

refactorings.summary: The file has good structure but needs significant refactoring for maintainability and testability. Key improvements: (1) Introduce Repository and Strategy patterns to separate database/payment concerns, (2) Extract validation functions for better testing, (3) Replace console.error and boolean returns with structured error handling, (4) Extract configuration constants to module level with proper typing, (5) Eliminate duplicate subscription validation logic, (6) Add proper decimal handling for monetary calculations, (7) Consider Value Objects for sensitive data. These changes would dramatically improve testability (addressing the NO TESTS warnings throughout) and follow SOLID principles.

recommendations.description: Replace raw credit card data handling with payment gateway tokenization (Stripe/Braintree). The current implementation stores and processes sensitive PCI data insecurely, violating PCI-DSS compliance requirements. This poses severe security and legal risks.

Implement comprehensive test suite for all payment processing functions. Zero test coverage on financial logic is unacceptable for production. Priority areas: payment validation, pricing calculations, subscription upgrades, and feature access control.

Fix critical date validation bug in card expiry check. Cards expiring in a given month are valid through the last day of that month, not the first day. This bug will incorrectly reject valid payment cards.
Add try-catch blocks around all JSON.parse operations to prevent application crashes from malformed database data. Currently, corrupted feature data will crash the entire application.

Implement transaction rollback mechanism to prevent charging users without granting subscriptions. If upgradeUserSubscription fails after payment succeeds, users will be charged but not receive premium access.
Implement Luhn algorithm for credit card validation and add numeric validation for CVV fields. Current validation only checks length, allowing invalid card numbers to pass through.

Introduce Repository Pattern for database operations and Strategy Pattern for payment gateway to improve testability and maintainability. This separation of concerns will enable dependency injection and make the code testable.

Implement caching layer for subscription data. Database queries are executed on every hasFeatureAccess call, which could be called frequently. Cache with appropriate TTL will significantly improve performance.

Extract configuration constants (pricing, tax rates, features) to module level with proper typing. Replace console.error with structured logging framework for better production monitoring and debugging.
Eliminate code duplication between hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription. Extract shared subscription validation and retrieval logic into reusable functions to ensure consistency.
